lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Skill consolidation: theorems about lines and angles

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The angles are congruent because they are opposite in position.
Vertical angles are congruent by definition.
The two lines are parallel, forcing the angles to match.
Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so both have the same measure.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 35°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 23° and 58°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 126°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 36. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 36, and it is parallel to the third side
18, and it is perpendicular to the third side
72, and it is parallel to the third side
18, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent, after constructing the bisector of the apex angle. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The base angles look equal in the diagram.
All triangles have congruent base angles.
The bisector is perpendicular to the base by definition.
The two smaller triangles are congruent by SAS, so their corresponding base angles are congruent.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 40°. Find the measure of the corresponding angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 63° and 35°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 35°. Find the consecutive angle.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 16. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 16, and it is parallel to the third side
32, and it is parallel to the third side
8, and it is parallel to the third side
8, and it is perpendicular to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The diagonals are perpendicular, which forces bisection.
Alternate interior angles give two pairs of congruent angles, and the opposite sides are congruent, so the triangles formed are congruent by ASA.
The diagonals are congruent, so they must bisect each other.
Every quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other.
